findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows five electrical transformer pads positioned on the site: west of Building 1 (northwest), southwest of Building 2 (west), east of Building 4 (center/east), east of Building 6 (east), and west of Building 8 (southwest). The transformer locations are clearly labeled with callout boxes and rectangular symbols. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows building footprints and overall site layout. However, no horizontal clearance dimensions are shown between any of the transformer pads and the building foundations or walls. The plans lack any notation, dimension line, or measurement indicating the distance from transformer pads to the nearest building structure. The Utility Notes on Sheet 21 state that "Contractor shall verify horizontal and vertical location of existing utilities prior to construction" and "notify engineer of any conflicts/discrepancies prior to installation," but this is a general directive rather than a demonstration that the 5-foot minimum clearance has been verified and documented on the plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires that building foundations maintain minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities (including transformer pads). The burden of demonstrating compliance is on the applicant through the site plan documentation. Presence of transformer pads on the plan combined with absence of clearance verification constitutes missing required information. The transformer locations are shown but no evidence is provided that they maintain the required 5-foot separation from buildings. Without dimension callouts, clearance arcs, or specific distance notations on the plans, it cannot be confirmed that this requirement has been addressed. The general contractor verification note is inadequate as a substitute for plan-based documentation of compliance.
findings.comment: Electrical transformer pads are shown on the preliminary electrical design plan near Buildings 1, 2, 4, 6, and 8, but no horizontal clearance dimensions or verification are provided demonstrating that they maintain the required 5-foot minimum distance from building foundations. Add clearance dimensions or notes on the electrical plan confirming that all transformer pads are positioned at least 5 feet from the nearest building structure.

applicableAreas: Retaining walls shown along site perimeter (north, east, south boundaries)
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) identifies multiple retaining wall segments throughout the site: a concrete retaining wall in the northeast corner along the biofiltration/detention pond, an existing retaining wall to be replaced along the entire eastern edge behind Buildings 5 and 6, and concrete retaining walls along the southern perimeter behind Buildings 7 and 8. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric lines forming a perimeter loop around the buildings, with the main lines running along the outer edges of the site where the retaining walls are located. However, no clearance dimensions are documented between the underground electric line routing and any of the retaining wall locations. No notes indicate that the required 5-foot separation has been verified. Sheet 38 (Wall Plan) would contain detailed wall dimensions and sections but was not reviewed in detail for this analysis.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires that permanent structures (including retaining walls) maintain minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric duct banks. The site plan shows both retaining walls and electric line routing in proximity to each other, but provides no documentation that this clearance requirement has been addressed. The absence of clearance dimensions or verification notes is a deficiency—required information is missing from the plans. While the general contractor verification notes reference utility coordination, they do not substitute for plan-based documentation showing that the clearance requirement has been satisfied.
findings.comment: Retaining walls are shown on the site plan around the perimeter (north, east, and south edges) and underground electric lines are routed near these locations, but no clearance dimensions or verification are documented showing that the required 5-foot minimum separation from duct banks is maintained. Provide clearance dimensions or notes on the electrical plan confirming that all retaining wall structures are positioned at least 5 feet from underground electric facilities.

applicableAreas: Electrical pull box locations distributed throughout site perimeter
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly identifies eight electrical pull box locations distributed around the site perimeter using callout boxes labeled 'Electrical Pull Box' with leader lines pointing to small nodes on the blue underground electric lines. Pull boxes are positioned: near the transformer pad west of Building 1, south of Building 2, west of Building 8, north of Building 3, east of Building 5, east of Building 6, and south of Building 7. However, the plan provides no dimension callouts, clearance arcs, or written notes indicating the horizontal distance of these pull boxes from property lines or from adjacent site features (buildings, walls, driveways, etc.). Specifically, no documentation is provided showing that pull boxes are inside the property line and maintain 5 feet clearance from all sides as required.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires that pull boxes be located inside the property line and maintain 5 feet clearance from all sides. The location of pull boxes on the plan is noted, but the specific clearance requirements are not documented. Without dimension callouts or verification notes showing that each pull box is inside the property line and maintains the required 5-foot separation, compliance cannot be confirmed. The absence of this required information on the plans constitutes a deficiency.
findings.comment: Electrical pull boxes are shown on the preliminary electrical design plan in eight locations around the site perimeter, but no clearance dimensions or verification are provided demonstrating that they are located inside the property line and maintain the required 5-foot minimum distance from all sides. Add clearance dimensions or notes to the electrical plan confirming each pull box location complies with the minimum distance requirements.

applicableAreas: Water line utility tap public plan and profile crossing location
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) shows both a plan view (top portion) and a profile view (bottom portion) for the proposed water line labeled 'Wtr-Ln-A' connecting to an existing 8-inch water main. The plan view (Block 2) clearly depicts a proposed underground electric line marked with the symbol '- E -' in the legend defined as 'Proposed Underground Electric.' This electric line is drawn crossing over the water utility lines in the plan view, positioned to the east of the meter vault. However, the profile view (Block 1) does not show the electric line crossing, nor does it document any vertical clearance dimension at this crossing location. While the plan view demonstrates that the crossing occurs, there is no horizontal separation distance documented at the crossing point. The profile shows water line flowline elevations but omits the electrical facility from the profile section entirely, leaving the vertical relationship completely undocumented.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires electric conduit routing to maintain minimum 12 inches (1 foot) horizontal clearance from water lines when crossing perpendicularly. The site plan documentation shows an electric line crossing water utility lines in plan view, confirming that a crossing condition exists. However, the plans provide no dimension callout or note documenting the horizontal clearance at this crossing point. The requirement is to show separation of at least 12 inches horizontally, and this required information is absent from the submitted plans. Required information is missing—specifically, the horizontal separation distance at the crossing is not documented. This is a deficiency per the standard that 'required information is absent from the plans (missing elements are deficiencies).'
findings.comment: Proposed underground electric line is shown crossing proposed water lines on the utility tap plan (Sheet 20, plan view), but no horizontal clearance dimension is documented at the crossing point. Provide a plan dimension or detail note showing that the electric conduit maintains at least 12 inches horizontal clearance from the water line at this crossing location.

applicableAreas: Proposed wastewater service lines and internal utility routing
findings.observation: Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) shows proposed wastewater lines (marked with 'WW' and purple/magenta coloring) routed through the central drive aisle of the property, branching to individual buildings to service the 39 units. The plan identifies a 'Duplex Grinder Pump Lift Station' in the northwest corner and '6" Cleanout' locations throughout. Sheet 20 shows the public water line profile and plan, with the proposed underground electric line ('E' symbol) visible in the plan view crossing through the same central utility corridor where wastewater lines are located. While the wastewater lines are clearly shown on Sheet 19 and the electric routing is shown on Sheet 20, no plan sheet provides documented horizontal clearance dimensions between the proposed electric conduit and the proposed wastewater service lines. The utility notes on both sheets (Blocks 16/Sheet 19 and standard Block 8/Sheet 20) contain only general contractor verification directives without specific clearance dimension documentation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires electric conduit routing to maintain minimum 12 inches (1 foot) horizontal clearance from wastewater lines when crossing perpendicularly. The site plan documents show proposed wastewater lines and proposed electric routing through the same general utility corridors and crossing areas, confirming that crossings will occur. However, no sheet provides documented horizontal clearance dimensions at these crossing points. Required information (horizontal separation distances of at least 12 inches at each crossing) is absent from the plans. This constitutes a deficiency per the standard that 'required information is absent from the plans.'
findings.comment: Proposed underground electric conduit is routed through the same utility corridors as proposed wastewater service lines, indicating crossings will occur, but no horizontal clearance dimensions are documented at the crossing locations. Provide plan dimensions or detail notes demonstrating that electric conduit maintains at least 12 inches horizontal clearance from wastewater service lines at all crossing points.

applicableAreas: Water utility tap connection area and internal distribution
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) provides both a plan view and a profile view for the proposed water line utility connection. The plan view (Block 2) clearly shows a label '- E -' (representing Proposed Underground Electric per the legend) crossing through the utility tap area east of the meter vault, intersecting with the proposed water line routing. A notation labeled 'Proximity Call' appears on the plan view but provides no specific measurement or clearance dimension. The profile view (Block 1) shows the water line ('Wtr-Ln-A') with flowline elevations documented at key locations (FL 8" = 674.33' at the entry point, and FL 8" = 671.42' and FL Out 6" = 671.42' near the meter vault). However, the profile view does NOT show the proposed underground electric line crossing, meaning the vertical clearance between the water line and the electric line at the crossing point is completely undocumented. The 'Proximity Call' label appears to be a placeholder for coordination but contains no dimensional information.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires that water lines crossing underground electric facilities maintain minimum 1 foot (12 inches) vertical clearance. The burden of demonstrating compliance is on the applicant through plan documentation. Sheet 20 plan view indicates that an electric crossing will occur (shown by the '- E -' line), and the 'Proximity Call' notation suggests the designer was aware of a proximity concern. However, the profile view—which is the correct tool for showing vertical clearance at utility crossings—completely omits the electric line from the section. No vertical clearance dimension, arc, or note documents the separation at this crossing. The applicant has failed to demonstrate compliance with the vertical clearance requirement. This is a clear deficiency: required information (vertical clearance dimensions at the water-electric crossing) is absent from the plans, and missing elements are deficiencies per the evaluation standards.
findings.comment: Proposed water line crosses proposed underground electric line on the utility tap public plan (Sheet 20), but the vertical clearance between the facilities at the crossing point is not documented in the profile view. Add the proposed electric line to the profile view and provide a vertical clearance dimension demonstrating that the water line maintains at least 1 foot minimum vertical clearance from the underground electric facility at the crossing location.

applicableAreas: Utility corridors where Austin Water (water/wastewater) and non-AW infrastructure (electric, storm drain) run in proximity
findings.observation: The site plan documents show multiple utility types routed through similar areas of the property: Sheet 19 shows water (W) and wastewater (WW) lines (Austin Water infrastructure) routed through the central drive aisles; Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines (non-AW infrastructure) forming a perimeter loop; Sheet 20 indicates an electric crossing over water facilities. The plans do not provide any dimension callouts, notes, or specifications documenting the horizontal separation distances between Austin Water infrastructure and non-AW infrastructure (particularly electric) in the utility corridors. UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires 5 feet minimum horizontal separation between Austin Water mains and all other non-Austin Water infrastructure, with an exception allowing 3 feet for residential service lines only. No plan view or detail shows measured separations meeting either the 5-foot requirement or the 3-foot residential exception with supporting documentation of which requirement applies and at what locations.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum horizontal separation of 5 feet between Austin Water infrastructure and all other non-Austin Water infrastructure to maintain trench integrity, with an exception allowing 3 feet for residential service lines only. The site plan shows both Austin Water utilities (water and wastewater) and non-AW utilities (electric and storm drain) sharing utility corridors. However, no plan view provides documented separation distances between these utilities. The plans lack dimension callouts, notes, or specifications indicating that either the 5-foot standard separation or the 3-foot residential service line exception has been verified and applied. Without plan-based documentation of these required separations, compliance cannot be confirmed. This is an unclear determination because the available evidence is insufficient to verify that the requirement is met.
findings.comment: Water and wastewater utilities from Austin Water are routed through the site in proximity to non-Austin Water infrastructure (electric and storm drain), but no separation distances are documented on the utility plans showing compliance with the minimum 5-foot horizontal separation requirement or the 3-foot residential service line exception. Provide dimension callouts or notes on the utility plans documenting that Austin Water infrastructure is separated from non-AW infrastructure by at least 5 feet (or 3 feet if residential service lines), as required.

applicableAreas: Proposed electric utility crossing water facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) shows a proposed underground electric line (marked '- E -' in the legend, defined as 'Proposed Underground Electric') crossing the proposed water line in the plan view east of the meter vault area. The crossing is indicated by the intersection of the electric line graphic with the water line graphic on the plan portion of the sheet. However, no detail sheet, profile view, or note on Sheet 20 or any related sheet reviewed documents or specifies concrete encasement requirements at this crossing point. Specifically, there is no detail showing 2-inch concrete encasement extending minimum 24 inches on either side of the crossing, nor is there any note referencing Austin Energy Design approval of the crossing configuration. The utility notes on Sheet 20 (Block 8) contain only general contractor verification directives and do not address the specific encasement requirement for electric conduit crossings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A specifies that when electric conduit crosses other utilities, it shall have 2-inch concrete encasement extending minimum 24 inches on either side of the crossing point, or encasement shall be verified as not required through Austin Energy Design approval. The site plan documents show an electric crossing occurring (Sheet 20 plan view), but no detail, note, or reference documentation is provided showing either: (1) the concrete encasement specification, or (2) written confirmation from Austin Energy Design that encasement is not required. Required information is missing from the plans. This is a deficiency because the applicant has not documented either the encasement detail or the design approval that would exempt this crossing from the encasement requirement.
findings.comment: Proposed underground electric line is shown crossing proposed water utility line on Sheet 20, but no concrete encasement detail or Austin Energy Design approval documentation is provided. Either provide a detail showing 2-inch concrete encasement extending minimum 24 inches on either side of the electric/water crossing, or provide written confirmation from Austin Energy Design that encasement is not required for this crossing.

applicableAreas: Fire demand meter vault area and surrounding utility infrastructure
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) identifies a structure labeled '8' Fire Demand Meter in 8' x 12' Vault' on the plan view west of the property entrance. The vault is shown with its footprint on the plan and appears to connect to the proposed water line at the tap location. Sheet 19 shows various utilities (water, wastewater, electrical) routed through the site in proximity to this vault area. However, no plan view or detail on either sheet documents or verifies that an exclusive 5-foot space exists around and under the vault structure, free of other underground utilities, appurtenances, or structures. UCM § 2.9.1.A.4 requires Austin Water vaults to maintain 5-foot exclusive space around and under the vault; no plan notation, dimension callout, or specification confirms that this requirement has been addressed or verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.A.4 requires that Austin Water vaults maintain required 5-foot exclusive space around and under the vault structure, with no other underground utilities, appurtenances, or structures allowed to encroach within this zone. The vault location is identified on the plan, and its general footprint is shown, but the plans provide no documentation that this exclusive space requirement has been verified or is being provided. Without dimension callouts or notes showing the 5-foot exclusion zone and confirming that no other utilities encroach within it, compliance cannot be confirmed from the available plan documentation. This is unclear because the plans lack sufficient information to verify the exclusive space requirement.
findings.comment: Austin Water fire demand meter vault (8' x 12' structure shown on Sheet 20) is depicted on the utility tap plan, but no exclusive 5-foot space around and under the vault is documented on the plans. Provide dimension callouts or notes on the utility plan confirming that the vault maintains the required 5-foot exclusive space with no other utilities or structures encroaching within this zone.

applicableAreas: Building exterior walls where electrical meters are mounted in relation to transformer pad locations
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) identifies electrical meter locations on each building's exterior walls: Building 1 south side, Building 2 south side, Building 3 north side, Building 4 north side, Building 5 east side, Building 6 south side, Building 7 south side, and Building 8 south side. Blue branch lines connect from the main underground electric line network and transformer pads to these meter locations. However, the plan provides no dimension callouts, sight line indicators, arrows, or notes documenting that each meter location: (1) is on the first floor or ground level, or (2) is within sight of the corresponding transformer location as required. While transformer locations are shown separately from meter locations, no visualization or notation demonstrates the sight line relationship or confirms that meters are within line-of-sight of their respective transformers.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 requires that electric meters be located on first floor or ground level and within sight of the Austin Energy transformer. While Sheet 21 shows both meter and transformer locations on the site plan, it provides no documentation confirming that: (1) all meters are at first floor or ground level (the plan does not show building sections or elevations for meter height), or (2) sight lines from each meter to its transformer are unobstructed. Without specific notation, sight line diagrams, or elevation details confirming these requirements, compliance cannot be verified from the submitted plans. This is unclear because the available plan documentation is insufficient to confirm that the meter location requirements are being met.
findings.comment: Electrical meters are shown on building exterior walls (Sheet 21), but no documentation is provided confirming that each meter is located on the first floor or ground level and within line-of-sight of its corresponding transformer. Provide notes or details on the electrical plan documenting the meter height and sight line relationship to each transformer.
